hints: Let $X \sim \mathrm{B}(5, 0.75)$ be the number of completions in 5 days.
The condition 'at least three times' means $X \ge 3$, so sum $X = 3, 4, 5$.
walkthrough: Let $X$ denote the number of days Jake completes the puzzle out of $n = 5$ days.

Since daily attempts are independent with constant probability $p = 0.75$:
$$X \sim \mathrm{B}(5, 0.75)$$
We want the probability that he completes it at least three times: $\mathrm{P}(X \ge 3) = \mathrm{P}(X = 3) + \mathrm{P}(X = 4) + \mathrm{P}(X = 5)$.

hints: Kenny completed the puzzle on Sunday.
If he completed Sunday, the probability he fails Monday is $1 - 0.8 = 0.2$.
If he fails Monday, the probability he fails Tuesday is $1 - 0.6 = 0.4$.
Use the complement rule: $\mathrm{P}(\text{at least one}) = 1 - \mathrm{P}(\text{fails both Monday and Tuesday})$.
walkthrough: We want to find the probability that Kenny completes the puzzle on at least one of Monday or Tuesday, given that he completed it on Sunday.
Let $C$ denote completing the puzzle, and $C'$ denote not completing it.

We are given:
- $\mathrm{P}(C_{n} \mid C_{n-1}) = 0.8$, so $\mathrm{P}(C'_{n} \mid C_{n-1}) = 1 - 0.8 = 0.2$
- $\mathrm{P}(C_{n} \mid C'_{n-1}) = 0.6$, so $\mathrm{P}(C'_{n} \mid C'_{n-1}) = 1 - 0.6 = 0.4$

Method 1: Complement approach (Most efficient)
The only outcome where Kenny does not complete the puzzle on at least one day is if he fails on BOTH Monday and Tuesday ($C'_{\text{Mon}} \cap C'_{\text{Tue}}$):
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{neither}) = \mathrm{P}(C'_{\text{Mon}} \mid C_{\text{Sun}}) \times \mathrm{P}(C'_{\text{Tue}} \mid C'_{\text{Mon}}) = 0.2 \times 0.4 = 0.08$$
Subtract from 1:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{at least one}) = 1 - 0.08 = 0.92$$

Method 2: Summing successful paths
- Completes Mon and Tue: $0.8 \times 0.8 = 0.64$
- Completes Mon, fails Tue: $0.8 \times 0.2 = 0.16$
- Fails Mon, completes Tue: $0.2 \times 0.6 = 0.12$
Sum: $0.64 + 0.16 + 0.12 = 0.92$.
